free_tier.stated: No quota of its own. It multiplies the 1TB item limit by however many versions you PUT. 'Saved versions will be placed in history/files/$key.~N~'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free (history files are served through the same item path)

tooling: raw IAS3 PUT header; rclone does not expose it, so a thin curl/requests shim is needed
chaining: A 20TiB cold archive can be stored as ~20 versions of a 1TB item if the payload changes, or used as a free append-only version store per key. Combined with x-archive-cascade-delete:1 for cleanup.
limits_note: For multipart the header must be set at multipart-complete time; history files are not exposed by rclone's listing, so you must enumerate history/files/ yourself; each version re-enters the per-item queue.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Unofficial-ish surface: documented but not exposed by any major client, so it is untested at scale and easy to orphan copies with.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
